 KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 Indian bowlers on top as New Zealand lost five wickets before reaching 100 runs in the 1st ODI. 
 Rohit Sharma pulled off a diving effort on the field to run out Daryl Mitchell in the 1st ODI. 
 Fans hailed the India veteran for setting fitness goals on the pitch at 39. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Rohit Sharma sets fitness goals: India veteran runs out Daryl Mitchell with a diving effort
 New Zealand batters struggled to find their ground right from the off in the 1st ODI of the five-match series in Auckland on Wednesday as Arshdeep Singh and Gurnoor broke the backbone of the Black Caps' batting.
 The hosts lost half of their side before even reaching the 100-run mark as they were simply outclassed on home conditions. It was surprising, considering how Auckland is known to be a venue that produces high-scoring games , primarily due to its short boundaries . 
 To add salt to their wounds, the Black Caps lost their most dangerous batsman, Daryl Mitchell, early in the innings courtesy of a brilliant fielding effort from a 39-year-old Rohit Sharma. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In the 22nd over of the match, Mitchell was slowly building his innings but a miscommunication with Glenn Phillips ended his journey in the first ODI.
 As he tried to take a quick single, Rohit Sharma showed great reflexes as he picked up the ball near short-leg and threw it directly at KL Rahul with a diving effort. Rahul made no mistake in collecting the ball and dislodging the bails to dismiss New Zealand's danger man.

 Fans react as Rohit Sharma pulls off a diving effort to run out Daryl Mitchell
 Fans were understandably elated after watching Rohit Sharma's fielding efforts, with many taking shots at the 39-year-old's critics. The India veteran has often been questioned about his fitness, which has led to doubts over whether the seasoned campaigner will be able to play until the ODI World Cup next year.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MORE:  Rohit record in Auckland: How Hitman has performed at Eden Park 
 Rohit Sharma shows he is ready for 2027 ODI World Cup
 Rohit Sharma's future in international cricket has come under the scanner on multiple occassions in the past few years, especially since he announced retirement from T20Is in 2024 and then from the Test format in 2025.
 Questions have been raised about whether Sharma can continue till the next ODI World Cup, which will be held in Africa in October and November 2027. More than Sharma's form it was his fitness that has been cited to dismiss his chances at the next World Cup.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, time and again, the veteran star has shown that neither his form nor his fitness is a concern. Sharma has worked on his fitness and it clearly shows on the field and his fielding effort on Wednesday will now put all rumours to rest regarding his participation at the 2027 ODI World Cup.
